paras: The attempted lynching of Henry Atkins took place at Blythe station in Richmond County, Georgia, in late July 1900, when a mob met a sheriff bringing Atkins, a Black man charged with assault and robbery, to the county authorities. Atkins escaped unharmed when the sheriff and his lawyer put him aboard a passing train, and the Savannah Morning News reported the episode as a case of officers who "outwitted the mob."

About a month before the report, Atkins, described as "a negro," was charged with assaulting and robbing F. E. Tinsley, a merchant at Blythe station. On a Friday afternoon Sheriff Ivey of Glascock County arrested him at Boyd's tie camp in the eastern part of that county and brought him to Gibson, where he was jailed.

The next morning Ivey boarded the early train with his prisoner to hand him over to the Richmond County authorities. With them went Colonel E. J. Hawkins, whom Atkins had employed to represent him. When the train reached Blythe, a mob "determined to lynch him" was waiting. According to the report, Hawkins and Ivey saved his life by jumping aboard an east-bound train that "arrived in the nick of time."
The coverage does not say where Atkins was taken after the escape or how the charge against him was resolved, and no arrests of mob members are reported.

The only report found is a short item on page 8 of the Savannah Morning News of 1 August 1900, headed "Officers Outwitted the Mob." It names Atkins only as "a negro" charged with the crime, credits the "strategy" of the sheriff and the lawyer, and passes no judgment on the mob, whose members and size go unmentioned. No account of the episode was found in the Black press.

reader.title: Attempted lynching of Henry Atkins
bases: A mob at Blythe station met a sheriff and his Black prisoner and was 'determined to lynch him'; the prisoner escaped unharmed by train, so this was a threatened or attempted lynching, not a killing (A1).

Atkins was not killed: the sheriff and his counsel got him away from the mob by boarding an east-bound train (A1). The mob acted without authority on the pretext of an assault and robbery charge, but its size is not given (A1).
Only one report, a short item in the Savannah Morning News, was found; no Augusta paper, wire story or Black-press account turned up (A1).

accounts.label: Georgia news item (Savannah Morning News)
accounts.gist: Sheriff Ivey and Atkins's counsel took the prisoner by train toward Richmond County authorities; at Blythe a mob determined to lynch him met them, and they 'outwitted' it by jumping aboard an east-bound train.

framing.detail: Headlined 'Officers Outwitted the Mob,' the item credits the 'strategy' of the sheriff and lawyer, calls Atkins 'a negro' and treats the charge as the cause without comment on the mob.
